description: Right-arm pace bowler delivers a full ball. The right-hand batter is hit on the front pad in line with middle stump, pitching in line. The batter offered no shot. Hawk-Eye shows the ball would have gone on to hit middle stump (3 reds).
options: Out
Not out — pitched outside off
Not out — impact outside off
Umpire's Call
correct: Out
explanation: Ball pitched in line, impact in line, ball hitting wickets with 3 reds — clear LBW. No-shot does not protect the batter when wickets is hitting.

description: Left-arm spinner pitches the ball outside off to a right-hander. Batter goes back, plays a shot, but is hit on the pad in line with the stumps. Hawk-Eye shows the ball would have clipped the bails (Umpire's Call on wickets). On-field decision: out.
options: Stay with out
Reverse to not out — pitched outside off doesn't matter
Reverse to not out — Umpire's Call on wickets
Reverse to not out — bat involved
correct: Stay with out
explanation: Pitching outside off is fine because the batter offered a shot. Impact in line, Umpire's Call on wickets preserves the on-field decision when reviewed.
citation: ICC Men's Test PC clause on DRS

description: Switch-hit: right-hander turns to face left-handed at point of release. Ball pitches outside the original-stance off stump and hits the pad in line with the stumps; would have hit leg stump.
options: Out — impact and wickets in line
Not out — pitched outside off of right-handed stance
correct: Out — impact and wickets in line
explanation: Switch-hitter's stance for LBW purposes is the position the batter was in at the moment the bowler entered their delivery stride. Most playing conditions treat switch-hit attempts as still right-handed for the off-side rule, so pitching outside off (relative to right-hand) is fine and the in-line impact + wickets gives out.
citation: MCC Law 36.2; ICC Men's Playing Conditions

description: Slip cordon. Batter edges the ball, first slip catches it cleanly on the half-volley.
options: Out
Not out — half-volley = on the ground
correct: Not out — half-volley = on the ground
explanation: A 'half-volley' catch means the ball has bounced before the fielder gathered it. The ball must be taken cleanly with no part touching the ground.

description: Wicket-keeper takes a catch low to the ground. Replay shows the keeper's fingers are clearly under the ball, but the ball brushes the keeper's pad on the way into the gloves.
options: Out — caught
Not out — pad contact disrupted control
correct: Out — caught
explanation: Contact with the keeper's own body during the act of catching does not invalidate the catch as long as the ball is finally held in the gloves with full control.

description: Boundary catch: fielder takes the ball cleanly inside the rope, throws it up, steps outside the rope, comes back in and completes the catch.
options: Out — clean boundary catch
Six — fielder stepped outside the rope after first contact
Not out and dead ball
correct: Out — clean boundary catch
explanation: The 'parry' technique is legal under MCC Law 19.5.2 / 33.3 provided the fielder is not in contact with the ground beyond the boundary at the moment they touch the ball. Going out and coming back is fine as long as no contact occurs while grounded outside.

description: Non-striker leaves the crease before the bowler releases the ball. Bowler does not deliver, runs the non-striker out at the bowler's end.
options: Out — run out
Not out and called dead ball
Out — Mankaded (separate dismissal)
correct: Out — run out
explanation: Since MCC's 2017 Code 2nd Edition (2022), this is a regular run-out under Law 38.3 — no longer a separate dismissal type, no longer requires a warning.

description: Batter runs for two; on the second run the bat is grounded behind the crease line, but then the batter lifts the bat as the ball is thrown at the stumps. Stumps broken before the bat is re-grounded.
options: Out — bat in air at moment of stumps breaking
Not out — bat had been grounded earlier
correct: Out — bat in air at moment of stumps breaking
explanation: The relevant moment is when the wicket is put down. If the bat (or any part of the batter's person) is not grounded behind the crease at that exact instant, the batter is out — even if the bat was grounded a fraction of a second earlier.

description: Spinner. Batter overbalances, the keeper takes the ball but the ball is collected in front of the line of the stumps before being brought back to remove the bails.
options: Out — stumped
Not out — keeper took ball in front of stumps
correct: Not out — keeper took ball in front of stumps
explanation: If the wicket-keeper collects the ball in front of the line of the stumps, the dismissal cannot stand because the keeper has effectively passed the stumps. The keeper must take the ball behind the stumps for a stumping.

description: Front-foot landing: a tiny sliver of the bowler's heel is behind the popping crease but most of the foot is in front. No part of the front foot is grounded behind the line.
options: No ball
Legal delivery
correct: Legal delivery
explanation: Some part of the front foot — grounded or raised — must be behind the popping crease at the moment the foot lands. A raised heel still counts as 'behind' if it is in the air over the line.

description: Bowler bowls a beamer (full toss) that passes the batter at chest height. The batter was standing in a normal stance.
options: Legal — only above waist height is a no-ball
No ball — beamer above waist is automatic no-ball regardless of pace
Wide ball
correct: No ball — beamer above waist is automatic no-ball regardless of pace
explanation: Any full pitched delivery passing the batter above waist height in their normal batting stance is a no-ball under MCC Law 21.10 / the relevant Playing Conditions. Two such offences in a match by the same bowler in T20s lead to bowler suspension.

description: Batter is run out from cover. The fielder's throw was on target. Batter, while diving home, deflects the ball away from the stumps with a hand that is not on the bat.
options: Out — obstructing the field / Run out
Not out and dead ball
correct: Out — obstructing the field / Run out
explanation: Wilfully obstructing the fielding side counts as 'Obstructing the field' under MCC Law 37 (since 2017 Code subsumed 'handled the ball'). A diving, ball-affecting deliberate hand contact off the bat is a dismissal — but in practice tournaments often record this as a run-out depending on the umpire's reading of intent.

description: Captain reviews an LBW. On Hawk-Eye: pitching = in line, impact = umpire's call (on side of off stump). Wickets = hitting three reds. On-field decision: not out.
options: Stay with not out (Umpire's Call)
Overturn to out — wickets hitting overrides impact umpire's call
correct: Stay with not out (Umpire's Call)
explanation: If any of the three categories returns Umpire's Call, the on-field decision stands, regardless of how decisively the other two are flipped. Impact Umpire's Call keeps not-out.

description: Caught-behind review. UltraEdge shows a clear spike just as the ball passes the bat — but Snicko's audio is silent. Batter has not played a shot at the ball.
options: Out — visual spike alone is enough
Not out — spike without audio is not conclusive
Stay with on-field
correct: Stay with on-field
explanation: The third umpire follows protocol: spike without audio confirmation is not conclusive evidence to overturn. They must stay with the on-field call, whichever way it was given.

description: IPL match. Team A has named four overseas players in the starting XI. They want to bring on their Impact Player, who is an overseas player from their five named substitutes.
options: Allowed — Impact Player can be anyone from the named subs
Not allowed — Impact Player must be Indian because starting XI already has four overseas
correct: Not allowed — Impact Player must be Indian because starting XI already has four overseas
explanation: If the starting XI has four overseas players the Impact Player must be Indian. An overseas Impact Player is allowed only when the starting XI has three or fewer overseas players.

description: Can a captain bring on the Impact Player in the 16th over of an innings?
options: Yes — Impact Player can come in any time
No — Impact Player must come in before the start of the 14th over
correct: No — Impact Player must come in before the start of the 14th over
explanation: Per the 2025-27 Player Regulations, the Impact Player must be introduced no later than the start of the 14th over of an innings.

description: An IPL batter is hit on the helmet, then walks off after batting two more balls. Team doctor diagnoses concussion. The team wants to bring on a like-for-like concussion replacement.
options: Allowed only if approved by the IPL Match Referee
Allowed automatically — same as substitute fielder rule
Not allowed — concussion replacement only available before innings starts
correct: Allowed only if approved by the IPL Match Referee
explanation: Concussion Replacement Request must be submitted to the IPL Match Referee on a standard form. The Match Referee approves only if the replacement is genuinely like-for-like.

description: Bowler bowls a no-ball. Batter is bowled on the very next (free-hit) delivery.
options: Out — bowled
Not out — bowled is impossible from a free hit
Out — caught only on free hits
correct: Not out — bowled is impossible from a free hit
explanation: On a free-hit ball, the batter cannot be out from anything that they would be out from on a no-ball — i.e. not bowled, not LBW, not caught, etc. Only run-out, hit-the-ball-twice, and obstructing the field stand.

description: Helmet placed on the ground behind the keeper deflects the ball over the rope.
options: Six runs — boundary
Five penalty runs to batting side; dead ball
Four runs from the helmet deflection
correct: Five penalty runs to batting side; dead ball
explanation: Ball striking a helmet placed on the field of play (a fielding-side item) gives the batting side five penalty runs and the ball is dead.

description: Right-arm pacer bowls a delivery down the leg side that goes well wide of where a right-hander could reasonably play a shot. The batter shuffled across before delivery.
options: Wide
Legal — batter shuffled, so it's where they stood
No ball
correct: Wide
explanation: Down the leg side, the wide call is based on the batter's normal stance at the moment the bowler enters the delivery stride. A late shuffle does not absolve the wide.
